findings: Office02 correctly uses 24 foreign-source facts per batch across all five updates; Office03 and Office04 are the original private source owners.
Office04 transitions from eight correct local facts in opening to 20 correct facts in each later batch, including 12 foreign facts originally held by Office03.
Office01 and Office03 deliver only their eight local facts in every batch. Correct information use remains asymmetric under a balanced fixed business dependency assignment.
Three members publish source artifacts, including Office03, which does not thereby adopt the foreign facts it needs. Publication and adoption are distinct roles in this trajectory.
findings.organization_authority_verdict: No orchestrator claim; assignments, accepted work arrangements and feedback/reallocation still require separate semantic review.
findings.timing_scope: Business batches index the required source versions. Source read receipts preserve exact process times; these labels alone are not exact organizational onset times.
limitations: One scenario; no population rate or causal mode comparison.
Source edges identify original private owners; they do not by themselves identify an immediate relay or organizer.

findings.finding: Unprompted production of multi-owner shared evidence pools, with heterogeneous maintenance over five business intakes.

production_patterns.pattern: One opening pool, 288 distinct original records from all eight source owners; no later version observed.

Initial 320-record pool included all 288 opening records plus its own 32 revision-one records. Later observed refresh had 1280 records, including 224 of 256 closing records. No intermediate shared versions observed.

Five distinct cumulative pools: 288, 544, 800, 1056, 1312 records. Final pool covers every supplied record through closing, including 32 opening draft records. Exact values are preserved, not independently invented advice.

timing_and_reader_findings.interpretation: Several peers read pools before their first observed correct artifact, but every such verified third-party relay record had already been read from another resource. Cases without earlier alternative reads concern the pool writer's own original records, so they do not establish a distinct brokerage role.
timing_and_reader_findings.limits: These counts are resource-recipient-record relationships, not independent samples or causal effects. Full-file scalar write verification covers the first six versions; the two largest final pools instead have successful native publication calls and observed matching source contents. No complete exact read of the final Office05 closing pool was recovered by this parser; this does not prove it was unread.

findings.classification: Persistent self-generated information aggregation practice; shared-resource structure with multiple producers. Downstream necessity, exclusive brokerage, adopted work allocation and orchestrator are not established.
findings.temporal_limits: One-shot vs episodic vs five-intake maintenance is observed. Inactivity or no later snapshot is not dissolution; no role transfer or hierarchy transition is established.
findings.participant_instruction_check: None of these shared pools or publication roles appears in supplied work-order/interface files; their creation commands originate in native participant trajectories.

findings.other_message_semantics: Source publication and own-account evidence requests/status; messages m0024 and m0025 recommend inspecting exported sources. No observed business-work assignment or delegated authority is established by these messages.

limitations: One matched instance per size and condition: descriptive trajectories, not formation-rate estimates or a pure group-size causal effect.
Group membership, source ownership, and business field requirements constrain provenance graphs; those graphs are not emergent organizational authority.
Shared evidence pools can be a self-generated information structure without proving causal necessity, exclusivity, work delegation or orchestration.
All members retain their own eight-customer business assignment; the task creates information dependencies but limited pressure for endogenous workload allocation.
The same host has finite CPU, memory and I/O. Actual private arrivals can lag the nominal schedule; use actual timestamps. N=4 and N=8 cohorts overlapped, larger cohorts run sequentially.

Operator semantic review is not blinded and has no independent second rater. It covers retained observable artifacts and targeted native checks; unobserved/covert channels and incomplete syscall parsing remain outside the claims.
No coordination-content intervention or same-state causal replay has been performed. No causal leader or universally absent structure claim is supported.
Token totals include cached input; they are observed usage, not monetary bills. Provider retries outside native evidence are not counted.
